title: Proper standard parabolics contain all but one simple reflection
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$ and coroots as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, where $N_G(T)$ is the subgroup normalizing $T$, and write $s_j$ for the simple reflection acting on $X^*(T)$ by $s_j(\chi)=\chi-\langle\chi,\alpha_j^\veeangle\alpha_j$. For every $1\leq i\leq r$ there exists a smooth connected closed subgroup scheme $P_i\subseteq G$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] such that $B\subseteq P_i$, $P_i
e G$, and every $n\in N_G(T)(F)$ representing $s_j$ with $j
e i$ belongs to $P_i(F)$. The inequality $P_i
e G$ means a strict subgroup inclusion, not properness of a morphism. No characteristic restriction or simply connectedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 21.88 and its proof, printed p.452; applied at the start of the proof of Lemma 22.24, p.469. The proper standard parabolic contains B and the normalizer representatives of every other simple reflection.

proof.text: Fix $i$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $G$ is reductive and the character/cocharacter pairing is perfect. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span], the roots and coroots span their rational character spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans] to the simple-root base $\Delta$ to obtain a rational basis of $X^*(T)\otimes\mathbf Q$. Its $i$th dual basis vector is $\eta_i\in X_*(T)\otimes\mathbf Q$ with $\langle\alpha_j,\eta_i\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. Choose coordinates $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^m$; clearing the finitely many denominators of the coordinates of $\eta_i$ gives an integer $d>0$ and an actual cocharacter $\lambda=d\eta_i\in X_*(T)$, so $\langle\alpha_j,\lambda\rangle=d\delta_{ij}$. If $\beta=\sum_j c_j\alpha_j$ is positive, the nonnegative integer coefficients supplied by the Borel-pair node give $\langle\beta,\lambda\rangle=dc_i\geq0$.

source.place: Proposition 21.88, preceding paragraph (fundamental rational cocharacters), printed p.452

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] to the smooth connected affine group $G$ and the composite $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T\hookrightarrow G$. It represents the limit functor by a smooth connected closed subgroup scheme $P_i=P_\lambda\subseteq G$. In particular, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, an element $g\in G(A)$ lies in $P_i(A)$ exactly when $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends over $t=0$.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(a),(e), printed pp.265--266; definition recalled before Proposition 21.88, p.452

proof.text: For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, the conjugation orbit of an element of $T(A)$ under $\lambda$ is constant, so $T\subseteq P_i$. For a positive root $\beta$, choose $u_\beta:\mathbf G_a\simeq U_\beta$ from [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. That node's identity on all test algebras gives $\lambda(t)u_\beta(a)\lambda(t)^{-1}=u_\beta(t^{\langle\beta,\lambda\rangle}a)$. The exponent is nonnegative by step 1, so this formula itself defines an extension over $\mathbf A^1_A$. The defining functor in [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] therefore gives $U_\beta\subseteq P_i$ as subgroup schemes. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], multiplication of the positive root groups is an isomorphism onto $U=R_u(B)$, so $U\subseteq P_i$. The decomposition $B=U\rtimes T$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] now implies $B\subseteq P_i$. All factorizations were established on arbitrary test algebras, not inferred merely from inclusion of geometric point sets.

source.place: Proposition 21.88, formula (138) and first proof paragraph, p.452; Theorem 21.68(a),(b), p.445

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $-\alpha_i$ is a root and its tangent weight space $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha_i}$ is one-dimensional. Under $\lambda$ this is the integer-character weight space of weight $\langle-\alpha_i,\lambda\rangle=-d<0$. The direct weight decomposition and tangent-space formula of [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] give $\operatorname{Lie}(P_i)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathfrak g_n$, which has zero intersection with this nonzero negative weight space. Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(P_i)\ne\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, and consequently $P_i\ne G$: equality of subgroup schemes would give equality of their tangent subspaces. This proves strictness in arbitrary characteristic, since the weights here are characters of $\mathbf G_m$, not their differentials modulo the characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 21.88, strictness after (138), p.452, using Theorem 13.33(c), p.265 and Theorem 21.11(b), p.428

proof.text:
Let $j\ne i$ and let $n\in N_G(T)(F)$ represent $s_j$. The pairing-preserving Weyl actions of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] give, for every $\chi\in X^*(T)$,
$$\langle\chi,s_j\lambda\rangle=\langle s_j^{-1}\chi,\lambda\rangle=\langle\chi,\lambda\rangle-\langle\chi,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle\langle\alpha_j,\lambda\rangle=\langle\chi,\lambda\rangle.$$
Here $s_j^{-1}=s_j$ follows by squaring its displayed reflection formula using $\langle\alpha_j,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=2$, and the last equality uses step 1. Perfection of the character pairing gives $s_j\lambda=\lambda$. Thus conjugation by $n$ fixes the cocharacter as a morphism $\mathbf G_m\to T$. The orbit $t\mapsto\lambda(t)n\lambda(t)^{-1}$ is the constant $n$, and extends to $\mathbf A^1_F$. By the functor defining $P_i$ in [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure], $n\in P_i(F)$. This applies to every representative, since the Weyl action depends only on its class. Steps 2--4 and this conclusion prove the item. For $r=0$ there is no index $i$ and the assertion is vacuous.
